candidates.tagline: FIFA approved a World Cup training pitch next to a rattlesnake zone
candidates.story: Switzerland's FIFA-approved 2026 World Cup training base at San Diego Jewish Academy required the Swiss Football Association to mark a red 'SNAKE AREA' on their official facility map — because four species of venomous rattlesnakes inhabit the California canyon behind the pitch.
candidates.why_funny: FIFA planned a World Cup across North America without checking whether 'no venomous wildlife on the training pitch' was a reasonable expectation, forcing Switzerland to publish an official snake-exclusion zone as part of their training-camp layout.
candidates.alt: Aerial photo of Switzerland's World Cup training pitch in San Diego with a bold red overlay on the canyon hillside behind it reading 'SNAKE AREA' in large white text

candidates.tagline: Port authority builds world's largest soccer ball nobody can kick
candidates.story: Massachusetts Port Authority erected a 47.9-foot inflatable soccer ball at East Boston's Piers Park II — breaking the Guinness World Record — covered in corporate sponsor logos and available to view for four days as the authority's contribution to World Cup 2026 promotion.
candidates.why_funny: A port authority, not a football federation, responded to the World Cup by building a soccer ball the size of a four-storey building that you are not allowed to kick, covered it in sponsor logos, and put it next to the harbour.
candidates.alt: A person stands gazing up at a massive blue inflatable soccer ball plastered with corporate sponsor logos, with the Boston city skyline visible in the background and a banner reading 'WORLD'S LARGEST SOCCER BALL' at the base
